text:
Thomas Harley's goal with one second left in the first period came on a 1% chance, a shot from the point that should almost never go in. It put DAL up 2-0, and Columbus spent the rest of the night chasing a lead that a long-odds goal had built.

The scoreboard and the game told different stories. We put the CBJ-DAL contest at 53% for Columbus in "deserved to win" terms, meaning the share of simulated replays of every shot that the Blue Jackets take. They out-attempted DAL 52 to 34 and outhit them 33 to 10. Dallas took the first period, 1.44 expected goals to 0.69 (expected goals measure the quality of chances), then Columbus controlled the second. Jake Oettinger stopped 24 of 25, about 1.5 goals better than the shots he faced deserved. Jet Greaves made 14 saves on 16 shots and kept it close.

Damon Severson cut the lead to 1-2 early in the third, on a 20% chance, with Zach Werenski, who logged 28:00 and was drafted eighth overall in 2015 out of Michigan, picking up an assist. But Arttu Hyry scored with one second left to seal it for Dallas, assisted by Jamie Benn and Miro Heiskanen. Mikko Rantanen had opened the scoring on a first-period power play. We don't have records or streaks for either club in the facts, so we'll say only that Dallas took two points from a game its numbers say it didn't quite earn, and Columbus has a loss that its chances say was worth more.
